body.title: `uv lock --upgrade` writes a dead edge (`python_version < '0'`) that a lock-guided `uv lock` drops, so uv.lock flips
body.body:
When a lock forks on the Python version, `uv lock --upgrade` (or locking with no `uv.lock` yet) writes a dependency edge whose marker can never be true: ```toml { name = "beta", version = "2.0", source = { ... }, marker = "python_version < '0'" } ``` A plain `uv lock` that has to re-resolve against the existing lock, for example after the project's own `version` changed, writes the same resolution without that edge. Each form accepts the other's lockfile (`--dry-run` reports no changes), so a project whose tooling runs both gets the same one-line diff in `uv.lock` back and forth. We hit it on every release of a project where the release step re-locked with plain `uv lock` and the test step with `uv lock --upgrade`; in that project the dead edge is `build`'s dependency on `importlib-metadata` (`python_full_version < '3.10.2'`) inside the `>= 3.11` fork. Seen with uv 0.13.0 and 0.13.10 on x86_64 Linux. ### Reproduction (offline, generated wheels) ``` alpha 1.0 Requires-Dist: beta; python_full_version < '3.10.2' gamma 1.0 Requires-Dist: beta>=2; python_version >= '3.11' beta 1.0 beta 2.0 Requires-Python: >=3.11 ``` ```toml [project] name = "demo" version = "1.0.0" requires-python = ">=3.10" dependencies = ["alpha", "gamma"] [tool.uv] find-links = [""] no-index = true ``` 1. `uv lock` with no lockfile: alpha's dependencies include `beta 2.0` with `marker = "python_version < '0'"`. 2. Set `version = "1.0.1"`, run `uv lock`: the edge is gone. 3. `uv lock --upgrade`: the edge is back. The lock forks at 3.11. In the `>= 3.11` fork alpha's `python_full_version < '3.10.2'` requirement can't hold, and the from-scratch path keeps the edge with the marker simplified to false instead of dropping it. ### Expected The same resolution gives the same lockfile whichever path produced it. I'd expect the edge to be left out, as the lock-guided path already does.
Script that builds the wheels and runs the three steps (python3 repro.py <empty dir>) ```python """Probe: do tiny local wheels reproduce uv's dead `python_version < '0'` edge? Usage: python3 fixture_probe.py Prints the dead-edge count after a fresh lock, after a version change + plain lock, and after --upgrade, so the bump/gate flip is visible. """ from __future__ import annotations import subprocess import sys import zipfile from pathlib import Path def wheel(dist: Path, name: str, version: str, requires: list[str], requires_python: str | None = None) -> None: tag = f"{name}-{version}" meta = [f"Metadata-Version: 2.1", f"Name: {name}", f"Version: {version}"] if requires_python: meta.append(f"Requires-Python: {requires_python}") meta += [f"Requires-Dist: {r}" for r in requires] files = { f"{name}/__init__.py": "", f"{tag}.dist-info/METADATA": "\n".join(meta) + "\n", f"{tag}.dist-info/WHEEL": "Wheel-Version: 1.0\nGenerator: probe\nRoot-Is-Purelib: true\nTag: py3-none-any\n", } record = "".join(f"{p},,\n" for p in files) + f"{tag}.dist-info/RECORD,,\n" with zipfile.ZipFile(dist / f"{tag}-py3-none-any.whl", "w") as zf: for path, text in files.items(): zf.writestr(path, text) zf.writestr(f"{tag}.dist-info/RECORD", record) def project(root: Path, version: str, links: Path) -> None: (root / "pyproject.toml").write_text( "[project]\n" 'name = "demo"\n' f'version = "{version}"\n' 'requires-python = ">=3.10"\n' 'dependencies = ["alpha", "gamma"]\n' "[tool.uv]\n" f'find-links = ["{links.as_posix()}"]\n' "no-index = true\n", encoding="utf-8", ) def dead(root: Path) -> int: return (root / "uv.lock").read_text(encoding="utf-8").count("python_version < '0'") def lock(root: Path, *args: str) -> None: subprocess.run(["uv", "lock", "-q", *args], cwd=root, check=True) def main() -> None: work = Path(sys.argv[1]) dist = work / "dist" dist.mkdir(parents=True) wheel(dist, "alpha", "1.0", ["beta; python_full_version < '3.10.2'"]) wheel(dist, "gamma", "1.0", ["beta>=2; python_version >= '3.11'"]) wheel(dist, "beta", "1.0", []) wheel(dist, "beta", "2.0", [], requires_python=">=3.11") root = work / "proj" root.mkdir() project(root, "1.0.0", dist) lock(root) print("fresh lock:", dead(root)) project(root, "1.0.1", dist) lock(root) print("version change + plain lock:", dead(root)) lock(root, "--upgrade") print("then --upgrade:", dead(root)) print((root / "uv.lock").read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` Output with uv 0.13.10: ``` fresh lock: 1 version change + plain lock: 0 then --upgrade: 1 ```

body.title: Read `.python-version` files with a BOM or UTF-16 encoding
body.body:
## Summary

On Windows it's easy to end up with a `.python-version` file that isn't plain UTF-8. Windows PowerShell 5.1 writes UTF-16 LE with a BOM when you run `echo 3.12 > .python-version`, and some editors (older Notepad, for one) save UTF-8 with a BOM.

We were reading the file with a plain `read_to_string`. With UTF-16 that fails with an invalid UTF-8 error. With a UTF-8 BOM the BOM ends up in the request string, so `3.12` doesn't parse as a version.

This uses `uv_fs::read_to_string_transcode` instead, the same helper we use for requirements files. It detects the BOM, strips it, and converts UTF-16 to UTF-8. Plain UTF-8 files behave exactly as before.

## Test Plan

I added two tests to `python_find.rs`: `python_find_pin_utf8_bom` and `python_find_pin_utf16`. The UTF-16 one has a BOM and `\r\n` line endings, since that's what PowerShell writes.

    cargo test -p uv --test python python_find_pin_

Without the fix, the UTF-16 test fails with "stream did not contain valid UTF-8" and the BOM test fails its snapshot. With the fix both pass.

I also ran the rest of the `python_find` and `python_pin` tests locally, 55 in total. 50 pass. The other 5 fail the same way with or without my change, because they need Python versions I don't have on this machine (e.g. "Could not find Python 3.10 for test"): `python_find_project`, `virtual_empty`, `virtual_dependency_group`, `python_pin_compatible_with_requires_python`, and `warning_pinned_python_version_not_installed`.

I also tried it by hand with the rebuilt binary. `uv python find` and `uv python pin` both work with a UTF-16 file and a UTF-8 BOM file.

One caveat: I'm on macOS and haven't tried this on Windows, which is where people actually hit this. CI will be the first Windows run.

body.title: `--link-mode=clone` fails with ERROR_MORE_DATA on Windows ReFS Dev Drive
body.body:
### Summary

Installing `annotated-types==0.8.0` with `--link-mode=clone` consistently fails on a Windows ReFS Dev Drive with `ERROR_MORE_DATA` (`0x800700EA`).

Both the uv cache and the virtual environment reside on the same ReFS volume.

The issue is reproducible with both an existing cache and a newly created cache. Installing the same package with `--link-mode=copy` succeeds.

### Environment

- **uv:** `0.13.9 (6b2d39dcc 2026-11-17 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)`
- **Python:** CPython 3.15.2
- **OS:** Windows 11, build 26300
- **Architecture:** AMD64
- **Shell:** PowerShell 7.7.0
- **File system:** ReFS 3.14 (Dev Drive)
- **Cluster size:** 4096 bytes

### Steps to reproduce

On a ReFS Dev Drive (mounted as `V:` in this example), run the following commands using a previously unused cache directory and virtual environment:

```powershell
uv venv V:\uv-repro\new-env --python 3.15

uv pip install annotated-types==0.8.0 `
    --python V:\uv-repro\new-env\Scripts\python.exe `
    --cache-dir V:\uv-repro\fresh-cache `
    --link-mode=clone `
    --no-deps -vv
```

### Expected behavior

The package should be installed successfully using block cloning.

### Actual behavior

Dependency resolution and wheel preparation succeed, but installation fails when cloning `annotated_types/test_cases.py`:

```text
error: Failed to install: annotated_types-0.8.0-py3-none-any.whl (annotated-types==0.8.0)
  cause: Failed to clone `V:\uv-repro\fresh-cache\archive-v0\m7RAYF3xB4ouNmbR\annotated_types\test_cases.py` to
         `V:\uv-repro\new-env\Lib\site-packages\annotated_types\test_cases.py`
  cause: 有更多数据可用。 (os error -2147024662)
```

The localized error message corresponds to `ERROR_MORE_DATA` (HRESULT `0x800700EA`, Win32 error 234).

### Control experiment

Using the same cached wheel and a separate virtual environment, installation succeeds with `--link-mode=copy`:

```powershell
uv venv V:\uv-repro\copy-env --python 3.15

uv pip install annotated-types==0.8.0 `
    --python V:\uv-repro\copy-env\Scripts\python.exe `
    --cache-dir V:\uv-repro\fresh-cache `
    --link-mode=copy `
    --offline --no-deps -vv
```

Output:

```text
Installed 1 package in 14ms
 + annotated-types==0.8.0
```

### Additional findings

| Cache | Link mode | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Existing cache | `clone` | Failed |
| Newly created cache | `clone` | Failed |
| Newly created cache | `copy` | Succeeded |

Both failed installations consistently report the same file and error code.

The affected file, `annotated_types/test_cases.py`, has a logical size of 6310 bytes. On the ReFS volume with a cluster size of 4096 bytes, it occupies two non-contiguous, single-cluster extents.

Querying its extents in the newly created cache using `fsutil file queryExtentsAndRefCounts` produces the following results (column names translated into English):

```text
VCN: 0x0  Clusters: 0x1  LCN: 0x187e02  Ref: 0x1
VCN: 0x1  Clusters: 0x1  LCN: 0x187604  Ref: 0x1
```

Native Windows block cloning was also tested independently using Robocopy, with `/NOCLONE` as a control, and worked as expected on the same volume.

The underlying cause has not been identified. Reproduction has so far been confirmed on the environment described above.

## Summary

This PR adds `python3.15-dhi`.

I'm not touching 3.10-dhi for now. It was initially kept in #22773 because the hardened 3.10 image had its own lifecycle. While it is marked as [EOL 2026-10-31](https://github.com/docker-hardened-images/catalog/blob/main/image/python/debian-13/3.10.yaml#L18), images still appear to be published.

## Test Plan

DHI builds are skipped for fork PRs, so CI won't build the new image here – but it's a trivial change.

body.title: LenientRequirement missing-dot fixup rewrites requests==2.32.3* to requests==2.3.*
body.body:
### Summary

When `LenientRequirement` fixes a missing dot before `*` on a three-part version whose middle segment has two digits, it drops the leading digits and rewrites the version to a different release series. For example, `requests==2.32.3*` in `pyproject.toml` is rewritten to `requests==2.3.*` and resolves `requests==2.3.0` without warning by default (whereas single-digit `requests==2.2.0*` is rewritten to `requests==2.2.0.*` and resolves `requests==2.2.0`).

Minimal reproduction:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/example && cd /tmp/example
cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[project]
name = "example"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = ["requests==2.32.3*"]
EOF
uv pip compile pyproject.toml
```

Output:

```text
Resolved 1 package in 7ms
# This file was autogenerated by uv via the following command:
#    uv pip compile pyproject.toml
requests==2.3.0
    # via example (pyproject.toml)
```

(`uv lock` and `uv sync` on the same `pyproject.toml` also resolve and install `requests==2.3.0`.)

Expected `requests==2.32.3*` to be rewritten to `requests==2.32.3.*` (resolving `requests==2.32.3`) or rejected as an invalid version specifier, rather than silently resolving `requests==2.3.0`.

Verbose output (`uv pip compile pyproject.toml -v`):

```text
DEBUG Found workspace root: /tmp/example
DEBUG Adding root workspace member: /tmp/example
DEBUG Skipping `pyproject.toml` in `/tmp/example` (no `[tool]` section)
...
DEBUG uv 0.13.10 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
...
WARN Fixing invalid requirement by inserting missing dot (before: `requests==2.32.3*`; after: `requests==2.3.*`)
DEBUG Found static `requires-dist` for: /tmp/example
DEBUG Solving with installed Python version: 3.14.10
DEBUG Solving with target Python version: >=3.14.10
DEBUG Adding direct dependency: requests>=2.3.dev0, <2.4.dev0
DEBUG Found fresh response for: https://pypi.org/simple/requests/
DEBUG Searching for a compatible version of requests (>=2.3.dev0, <2.4.dev0)
DEBUG Found fresh response for: https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f7/51/7aa1e337862118bee783c0249debd64cb07b8fbdfef154b1e185754b02d5/requests-2.3.0-py2.py3-none-any.whl.metadata
DEBUG Selecting: requests==2.3.0 [compatible] (requests-2.3.0-py2.py3-none-any.whl)
DEBUG Tried 1 versions: requests 1
DEBUG marker environment resolution took 0.001s
Resolved 1 package in 3ms
# This file was autogenerated by uv via the following command:
#    uv pip compile pyproject.toml
requests==2.3.0
    # via example (pyproject.toml)
```

In `crates/uv-pypi-types/src/lenient_requirement.rs`, the `"inserting missing dot"` fixup uses `regex!(r"(\d\.\d)+\*").replace_all(input, r"${1}.*")`: because `+` is outside capture group 1, `2.32.3*` matches `(\d\.\d)` twice (`2.3` then `2.3`) and `${1}` retains only the last group (`2.3`).

### Platform

Linux 6.1.0-56-cloud-amd64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.13.10 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) and main (`e3e7c1eacb980339352a5ad69affcd3b6c206c92`)

### Python version

Python 3.14.10

We found this while fuzzing.

Credit: https://ucsbplse.github.io/
